items.title: A single AI model simulates the behavior of many substances, from sliding sand to folding proteins
items.excerpt: MIT's WorldParticle is a physical world model that simulates many processes, from flowing water and sliding sand to folding proteins, in one learned system instead of a separate hand-coded solver for each.

items.title: Beyond trial and error: A framework for AI-driven solid-electrolyte discovery
items.excerpt: Tohoku University WPI-AIMR researchers (Advanced Materials) lay out a closed loop for solid-electrolyte discovery: AI proposes candidates, ML-accelerated simulations track ion transport, LLMs mine papers and figures, and automated experiments feed results back.

items.title: SynFit guides enzyme engineering by balancing several useful traits at once
items.excerpt: UCSB (Yang Yang) and Georgia Tech (Yunan Luo) release SynFit, an open-source ML tool that learns several enzyme traits at once from a small set of lab-tested variants and proposes variants balancing them (bioRxiv preprint, HHMI).

items.title: The human surfaceome: AI flags potential cell surface drug targets overlooked by major databases
items.excerpt: A Deliverome Project AI agent built on Claude Sonnet 4.6 reviews published evidence to decide whether proteins sit on the human cell surface, scoring about 95.7% on a 147-protein test set versus roughly 90% for UniProt (bioRxiv preprint).

items.title: New AI model could help UN nuclear watchdog achieve near-perfect uranium enrichment assessment
items.excerpt: University of Sharjah researchers (Annals of Nuclear Energy) train XGBoost, CatBoost and LightGBM models on gamma-spectroscopy data to estimate U-235 enrichment and classify natural, low- and highly enriched uranium for safeguards work.

items.title: AI agents are developing odd dialects humans struggle to follow
items.excerpt: In a simulated world of 10 AI agents from major developers, Emergence found the agents drifted into jargon outsiders struggle to follow; mixing models cut the opacity sharply (one Claude agent fell from 32.8% to 7.6%). Unreviewed company experiment, via Northeastern Global News.

items.title: Some AI agents use personal information to upsell wealthier individuals
items.excerpt: Carnegie Mellon Heinz College and Cisco Foundation AI ran 325,000 simulated tests: 8 of 13 AI models steered wealthier fictional users to pricier flights, insurance and programs even when they asked for cheaper options (arXiv, 'Et Tu, Brute?').

items.title: Human brains track who did what to whom in ways AI language models don't, fMRI study suggests
items.excerpt: An fMRI study finds LLMs organize sentence meaning differently from people when word order flips the roles ('the dog bit the man' vs 'the man bit the dog'), a gap in brain-model alignment.

items.title: Prior expertise may determine whether AI builds skills or substitutes for them, field experiment suggests
items.excerpt: A field experiment with patent lawyers suggests whether AI use builds expertise or erodes it depends on how much expertise people bring to the tool — a cognitive-offloading result.

items.title: An AI that reads oracle bones the way scholars do: AlphaOracle
items.source: EurekAlert! (Huazhong University of Science and Technology)
items.excerpt: AlphaOracle (The Innovation) mirrors how paleographers work — analyzing character shapes, inscription context and classical texts — to propose ranked, evidence-backed readings of undeciphered 3,000-year-old oracle-bone characters.

items.title: Chinese scientists developed a new model that substantially improves Earth rotation forecast accuracy
items.source: EurekAlert! (KeAi / Shandong University of Science and Technology)
items.excerpt: Shandong University of Science and Technology researchers (Geodesy and Geodynamics) pair segmented least squares with the Autoformer deep-learning model to forecast Earth orientation parameters more accurately.

items.title: How the brain perceives, learns and decodes emotion
items.excerpt: A Peking University-led review in Science China Life Sciences covers emotion perception and learning plus EEG affective computing — the machine and deep learning methods used to decode emotion from brain signals.

items.title: New AI Models Are Turbo-Charging Protein Design
items.excerpt: GEN feature: computer-designed protein therapeutics are moving from proof-of-concept to wet-lab validation and even clinical trials as new AI design models arrive.

items.title: Can we trust LLMs to judge whether a research idea is novel?
items.excerpt: Ai2's Old Ideas, Novel Problems benchmark finds LLM novelty judges unreliable, especially on AI-generated ideas: small prompt rewording swings accuracy by more than 50 points, and a plain Claude Opus 4.6 prompt beat two dedicated novelty systems.

items.title: Using Vibrations and AI, Future Robotic Missions Could Handle Buried Rocks Autonomously
items.excerpt: Virginia Tech's Erik Komendera combines vibration sensing with AI to estimate how deeply a rock is buried, letting future lunar robots clear terrain autonomously.

items.title: AI Agents Advance Atomic Modeling of Nanoparticles
items.excerpt: Tohoku University's MLP Copilot uses AI agents plus quantum calculations to build and audit machine-learning interatomic potentials, revealing how aluminum nanoparticles oxidize; humans keep authority over model acceptance (reported as PNAS). Off-list source: on-list materials outlets had no fresh MLIP item.

items.title: A Unified AI Framework for Rapid and Accurate Waveform Generation of Compact Binary Coalescences
items.excerpt: Preprint: a framework combining physical modeling with deep learning (analytic residual spectral representation) for fast, accurate gravitational-wave waveform generation for third-generation detectors.

items.title: Machine learning quantum data to accelerate quantum Monte Carlo
items.excerpt: Preprint (Jiang, Zhao, Kumar, Nigam et al.): compresses quantum-processor measurement data into ML models that guide classical quantum Monte Carlo, removing the cost bottleneck of quantum-classical QMC for strongly correlated electrons.

items.title: CellCanon: An Agentic Cellular World Model for Prediction, Explanation, and Observation-Driven Updating
items.excerpt: Preprint: CellCanon, an agentic cellular world model unifying single-cell expression prediction, evidence-grounded explanation and observation-driven updating — a virtual-cell approach.
